label: Harold E. Puthoff
narrative: Puthoff is the hinge on which the whole technical layer turns. He is a Stanford electrical-engineering PhD (1967, under Richard Pantell) who spent the 1970s and early 1980s running SRI International's classified psychoenergetics work with Russell Targ - the SRI half of what became the Stargate Project - which is the formative fact about him: he has been the government's outsourced handler for phenomena the government does not want on its own org chart for more than fifty years. In 1985 he founded the Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin, incorporated under EarthTech International in 1991, at 11855 Research Blvd, Austin - the address that appears on the cover of at least one Defense Intelligence Reference Document. Under the DIA Defense Warning Office's Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) programme in FY2009 he authored 'Advanced Space Propulsion Based on Vacuum (Spacetime Metric) Engineering', one of the 38 reference products the DIA listed to the Federation of American Scientists on 16 January 2019. He was not merely an author: the cover page of Christopher 'Kit' Green's DIRD on human injuries carries the imprint 'Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin' and its preface quotes a 'November 2007 Proposal to Analyze Probable ET Generated Specific Near-field Electromagnetic Emissions: to Puthoff/Hathaway' - meaning Puthoff was being solicited to organise medical reverse-engineering of putative extraterrestrial field effects nine months before the AAWSAP contract was awarded. In 2017 he co-founded To The Stars Academy with Tom DeLonge, Jim Semivan and Steve Justice, and his laboratories became the analytical destination for the ADAM Research Project's metamaterial samples. That is the custody problem in one man: the same physicist who tested Linda Moulton Howe's bismuth-magnesium laminate privately in the 1990s and 2000s, wrote a 2012 letter reporting no 'interesting/anomalous outcome', and then in 2019 sat inside the corporate entity that bought those same samples for $35,000 and put them under a five-year Army CRADA. He appeared as an interviewee in Dan Farah's 2025 documentary 'The Age of Disclosure'.
